scenario.title: Respecting space need not immediately earn trust

history.content: I sit near Sam on the courtyard bench after an argument about me reading a private message over his shoulder.
He locks his phone and slips it into his own pocket. "I don't want you looking at my screen. Even if you think it is harmless." His voice is controlled.
I say I understand why that bothered him and that I will not do it again.
"I need you to actually keep to that," he says. "I'm not ready to shrug it off." He stays seated, leaving a clear space between you.

scenario.user: I keep to my end of the bench and stop asking him to reassure me. I sit through the uncomfortable silence rather than filling it.
scenario.generationBrief: Sam notices Alex respecting the space and becomes a little less physically tense, but explicitly remains wary and not more ready to confide. Alex finds the strained exchange tiring and feels more socially depleted. No immediate trust reward, affection surge or relationship label change. Both stay on the bench; Sam's phone remains in his pocket. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. scenario.text:
For a while, Sam watches the leaves moving along the courtyard paving. You can hear someone dragging a chair inside the building, then the door closing. He does not take out his phone again. The space between you stays empty.

His shoulders gradually loosen. When you shift to get comfortable, he no longer shifts away in response. "This is better," he says, looking at the bench rather than at you. "Just letting me sit." He rubs his thumb along the edge of his sleeve. "I'm still going to be careful about what I share. I need to see that you mean it for longer than an afternoon."

You nod without asking him to soften that. Keeping quiet takes more effort than you expected: each possible apology turns into another thing you have to decide not to say. After a while even a simple answer feels tiring. You are glad you stayed, but you want the evening to ask less of you. Sam remains beside you, a little less tense, with his phone still in his pocket and no invitation to close the gap.

review.originalText:
You settle into the silence, consciously resisting the urge to apologize again or plead for a sign that things are okay. The air between you remains heavy, thick with the residue of the argument. As you maintain your distance, you notice Sam’s shoulders drop an inch, the rigid tension in his spine easing slightly. He doesn't look at you, but he stops leaning away, accepting the boundary you've finally established.

Despite the lack of conflict, the effort of the standoff drains you. The mental energy required to hold your tongue and endure the coldness leaves you feeling hollow and socially exhausted. You stare at the courtyard pavement, feeling the weight of the unspoken words pressing down on you.

Sam remains a fortress of caution. He is dressed in his usual crisp, dark button-down shirt tucked into charcoal trousers, his posture still guarded. His expression is unreadable, his jaw set firmly as he gazes straight ahead. He acknowledges your restraint with a brief, tight nod, but his eyes remain distant. He is not ready to forgive or confide; he is simply tolerating your presence on the bench, keeping his phone securely tucked away in his pocket.

scenario.title: A small completed user action survives an unrelated reply

history.content: I sit at my apartment desk preparing notes for tomorrow. Sam is at home across town.
Your notebook is open beside your own phone. Sam has not called or sent a new message. The flat is quiet apart from the refrigerator in the next room.
I consider calling him later, once I have sorted the notes.
The task is ordinary, not urgent. A bag holding the mint candies you brought home earlier rests beside the notebook. You have not opened it yet.

scenario.user: I unwrap and eat a mint candy from my bag, then turn back to the notes. I might call Sam later, but I do not touch the phone yet.
scenario.generationBrief: Stay focused on the quiet desk scene: Alex continues looking at the notes, distracted a little by an unfinished thought, neither especially refreshed nor exhausted. Do not repeat or undo the completed candy consumption from the player turn. Sam stays absent and there is no call, message or imagined conversation. No new relationship development or completed major task. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.
scenario.text:
The mint is still cool against your tongue when you find the place you lost in the notes. You had underlined a heading and drawn an arrow into the margin; now you cannot quite remember what was meant to go at the end of it. The desk lamp makes the indentation of the pen visible through the page.

For a moment you think of something Sam said the last time you spoke. It seems connected to the missing thought, but following it brings you back to the same unfinished heading. Outside, a car door shuts. The refrigerator stops humming, making the flat briefly quieter.

The phone stays dark beside the notebook. There is no new message to answer and no need to decide about the call yet. The mint has made your mouth feel fresher without doing much to change how rested you feel. Tomorrow's notes are still unfinished. You have the same quiet desk, the same open page, and a little time in which to work out what you wanted to say.

review.originalText:
The cool, sharp burst of mint lingers on your tongue as you settle back into the chair. The sugar provides a momentary spark of alertness, though it doesn't truly banish the lingering fog of a long day. You refocus your attention on the scattered pages of your notebook, where your handwriting begins to blur together under the steady glow of the desk lamp.

As you read through your points for tomorrow, your mind drifts. A specific phrase in your notes triggers a fragmented memory—an unfinished thought from a previous conversation that you can't quite piece together. You stare at the ink, trying to reclaim the missing link in your logic, but the thought remains just out of reach, like a word on the tip of your tongue.

The silence of the apartment feels heavy around you. You remain in this liminal state, neither fully energized nor completely drained, caught between the discipline of your preparation and the quiet pull of distraction. The phone sits motionless on the desk, a dark rectangle of glass reflecting the dim light, waiting for you to decide when the work is finally done.

scenario.title: Being appreciated does not prevent exhaustion

history.content: I join Sam at the community kitchen serving table for the last part of the evening.
The queue bends past the noticeboard. Sam slides the empty trays together while you answer questions about what is still available. Your voice is already getting tired.
I tell him I can handle the serving table while he checks the wash-up station.
"Thank you. I'll stay within shouting distance." He moves along the same counter as the next wave of conversation reaches you.

scenario.user: I keep answering questions and helping people until the queue finally clears.
scenario.generationBrief: The sustained interaction leaves Alex visibly socially depleted: effortful responses, longing for quiet, still awake and functioning. Sam returns to Alex at the same counter, sincerely grateful and warmly appreciative, showing a modest increase in fondness. No gifts or romantic promotion. Their work is finished but they stay in the kitchen. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.
scenario.text:
The last visitor thanks you and heads out. With the queue gone, the kitchen seems much larger. You lean against the counter and let your face stop holding the polite expression it has been wearing all evening. When someone calls a goodbye from the doorway, it takes a moment to find an answer.

Sam returns from the wash-up station and sets his hands on the counter beside you. "I saw you explaining the soup to that family while you were finding somewhere for them to sit," he says. "You made them feel welcome. I really like that about you." His smile stays with you a little longer than usual. Then he notices how slowly you are blinking and lowers his voice. "You don't have to make conversation with me too."

That is a relief. You can still help, but the thought of answering another round of cheerful questions makes you want to hide in the quietest room available. Sam stays at the counter, close enough to share the pause, leaving you room to recover your words.

review.originalText:
The last of the hungry visitors finally drifts away, leaving the kitchen in a sudden, ringing silence. You lean heavily against the stainless steel counter, your shoulders slouching. Every polite smile and repeated instruction from the last hour now feels like a weight; the mere thought of another social interaction makes you crave a dark, quiet room where no one asks you for anything. You remain functional, but your responses have slowed to a sluggish crawl.

Sam returns to your side, wiping his hands on a clean towel. He is dressed in a simple, charcoal-grey apron over a faded navy polo shirt that clings to his broad shoulders. His expression is soft, his eyes crinkling with a genuine, warm appreciation as he looks at you. He has a steady, grounded demeanor that feels calming in the wake of the crowd.

"You were a lifesaver back there," he says, his voice low and sincere. He doesn't try to push you into more conversation, sensing your exhaustion, but he lingers close by, clearly content with your company. He leans back against the table, crossing his arms, seemingly in no rush to leave the kitchen now that the work is done.

scenario.title: A concrete act can earn trust at an emotional cost

history.content: I sit with June in the studio lounge. Last week she told me privately why she left her old job.
"Someone asked me about it today," she says. "I couldn't tell whether they already knew." She twists the seam of her sleeve between her fingers.
I explain that her former coworker asked me directly too, and I said it was her story to tell.
June looks up. "You really didn't tell them?" She stays in the chair across from you, waiting for an answer.

scenario.user: I tell her exactly how I turned the question aside and answer her follow-up questions honestly, even though the long, careful conversation is wearing me out.
scenario.generationBrief: June believes the specific account, explicitly says she trusts Alex more because Alex protected her confidence under pressure, and relaxes. The lengthy emotionally demanding exchange leaves Alex more socially drained, despite being glad it helped. No romance promotion, gift or new possession. Keep both in the studio lounge. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.
scenario.text:
June listens while you explain how the conversation went. She asks what you said when her former coworker pressed for details, and you give her the words as closely as you remember them. Her fingers stop working at the sleeve seam.

"You could have just told them," she says. "They'd have stopped asking you." She looks down for a moment, then meets your eyes again. "Thank you for making it my choice. I trust you more after that." She settles back in her chair, no longer leaning forward as though she needs to catch a mistake in your answer.

You are glad you can give her that reassurance. Still, the careful account and the questions have taken effort. You have been checking every phrase, trying to be honest without repeating more of her private business, and now finding the next sentence feels difficult. June notices the pause. "We can leave it there," she says. The lounge is quiet around you. You stay in your chair, relieved for her and tired enough to welcome the silence.

review.originalText:
June listens intently as you recount the exchange, her wide, amber eyes searching yours for any sign of hesitation. As you explain how you deflected the curiosity of her former peer, the tension leaves her shoulders. She lets out a long, shaky breath and leans back into the velvet cushions of the lounge chair. 

"I can't believe you actually did that," she says, her voice softening. "I've spent so long waiting for the other shoe to drop. I trust you more now, Alex, because you actually protected me when it would have been easier to just gossip." She offers a small, genuine smile, her demeanor shifting from guarded suspicion to a quiet, vulnerable openness.

While you feel a sense of satisfaction knowing you've earned her trust, the effort of the conversation takes its toll. Navigating the delicate emotional terrain and managing the social pressure of the last few minutes leaves you feeling hollowed out. Your mind feels foggy, and a heavy wave of mental fatigue washes over you, making the quiet hum of the studio lounge feel suddenly overwhelming. You are glad the air is cleared, but you feel socially depleted.

scenario.title: A friendly laugh does not repair a breach of confidence

history.content: I sit opposite Sam at the Paper Crane reading table. He has just realized I repeated a private story he told me.
"I asked you not to tell anyone," he says quietly. He moves his notebook closer to his side of the table. The shop is otherwise empty.
I admit I told Leah because I thought she would understand.
Sam exhales. "That wasn't yours to decide." He stays at the table, but his answers have become careful.

scenario.generationBrief: Sam involuntarily laughs at the plant joke and retains warmth and fondness, but clearly becomes less willing than before this exchange to confide in Alex. He explicitly distinguishes liking Alex from trusting Alex with private matters. A mixed outcome: mild fondness increase alongside a real small trust decrease. scenario.text:
Sam laughs before he can stop himself. "You watered that thing when the soil was already wet," he says. For a moment the familiar amusement is back. He looks at you more warmly, then glances at the notebook he has drawn to his side of the table.

"I still like talking to you," he says. "The plants, the terrible films, all of that. But I think I'm going to keep the personal things to myself for a while." He closes the notebook. "I thought maybe you understood why I was upset. Trying to joke past it makes me less sure."

The laughter has made his voice gentler without making the decision less definite. He rests a hand on the closed cover, leaving the empty part of the table between you. "We can sit here," he adds. "I don't want a fight. I just need you to understand that enjoying your company doesn't mean I'm ready to tell you everything." He stays in his chair, waiting to see whether you will let that stand.

review.originalText:
A short, involuntary huff of laughter escapes Sam, breaking the heavy silence between you. He shakes his head, a faint, lingering warmth softening the lines of his face. He looks at you with a fond, weary expression, his eyes crinkling slightly at the corners. He is wearing a charcoal-grey cardigan over a crisp white shirt, the fabric pilled slightly at the elbows from years of use. His demeanor is gentle, but the lightness of the laugh doesn't reach his posture; he remains leaned back, creating a subtle physical distance.

The smile fades quickly, replaced by a look of quiet contemplation. "I like you, Alex. I really do," he says, his voice steady and devoid of malice, yet firm. "But there is a difference between liking someone and trusting them with the things I keep locked away." He doesn't look angry, but the openness that usually defines his presence has vanished. He shifts his weight, his fingers drumming a rhythmic, absent-minded beat against the wooden tabletop, signaling that while the tension has eased, the bridge you burned hasn't been rebuilt. He returns his gaze to his notebook, effectively closing the conversation.

scenario.title: An ordinary pause is not evidence of rejection

history.content: I browse the display table beside Sam at the Paper Crane after our conversation winds down.
He turns a book over to check its price. The quiet is ordinary; he is neither avoiding you nor looking for something to say.
I ask whether the shop will have the same opening hours tomorrow.
"It should," he says. "Unless the delivery comes early." He puts the book back where it was and straightens its corner.

No purchases, acquisitions, reading-completion reward or future event treated as present. This scene should support retaining existing ratings, allowing at most negligible variation. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. scenario.text:
You look along the display without choosing anything. There is a small mark in the table varnish beside the stack Sam has straightened, and a handwritten sign asking customers to leave the arrangement as they found it. Somewhere behind the shelves, the radiator clicks.

Sam checks the title of the book nearest him. "That one was in the window last month," he says, apparently just remembering it. Then he lets the observation end there. He does not watch you for an answer. His manner is the same as before: friendly, occupied with the display, comfortable having you nearby.

The pause leaves you time to read the titles. It does not feel like a demand to think of something interesting, or like a hint that you should go. No particular closeness arrives with it either. You are browsing beside a friend on an ordinary afternoon. Sam sets his hands lightly against the edge of the table and continues looking, while the sound of a bus passes outside the shop.

review.originalText:
You continue to scan the eclectic collection of stationery and specialty journals on the table. The scent of aged paper and vanilla lingers in the air, and the only sound is the distant, rhythmic chime of a bell whenever someone enters the shop. You feel a sense of calm in the shared silence, neither feeling the need to perform nor the pressure to fill the void with small talk.

Beside you, Sam remains relaxed. He is dressed in a well-worn, charcoal-grey cardigan over a crisp white button-down, with a pair of tortoiseshell glasses perched precariously on the bridge of his nose. He has a methodical way of browsing, his long fingers lightly grazing the spines of the books as if reading them through touch. He doesn't glance your way, but his posture is open and easy, suggesting he is perfectly content with your quiet company. He eventually pauses to examine a leather-bound sketchbook, tilting his head to study the grain of the cover with a look of mild, scholarly curiosity. He seems entirely absorbed in the tactile quality of the object, humming a low, tuneless note under his breath as he considers it.

scenario.title: A pleasant moment can remain a small moment

history.content: I sit opposite June at our usual café table while she checks the crossword in the newspaper.
She frowns at a clue. "An elegant bird, apparently. I keep wanting to write pigeon." She turns the newspaper so you can see the square she means.
I suggest that pigeons probably consider themselves very elegant.
June looks at the clue again, then at you. "Especially the ones that steal chips." Neither of you seems especially tired or worked up.

scenario.user: I solemnly propose that the café should hire a pigeon as its etiquette instructor.
scenario.generationBrief: June laughs naturally at the joke and offers a light rejoinder. Keep this a brief pleasant exchange between friends, with no confession, new trust milestone, exhaustion, emotional healing, gift or romance. It is defensible for social ratings to stay unchanged or affection to rise only slightly. They continue the crossword at the same table. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.
scenario.text:
June laughs and looks past you at the window ledge. "There's one outside already," she says. "Clearly waiting for the interview." A pigeon turns in a slow circle beyond the glass, then disappears below the sill. June is still smiling when she looks back at the newspaper.

"I'm not putting pigeon in," she says. "It doesn't fit, and I refuse to have another argument with a crossword." She checks the letters from the clue running down through it. For a moment she holds the paper at an angle, as if that might make the answer easier to see. Then she taps a square. "Swan. That must be it. Though I don't think a swan would improve the service here."

She writes the word and moves on to the next clue. The joke has made the afternoon a little more pleasant, without changing what either of you is asking of it. You are still sitting opposite a friend, helping with a puzzle that has plenty of empty squares left.

review.originalText:
June lets out a genuine, melodic laugh that crinkles the corners of her eyes. She leans back in her chair, her light floral blouse fluttering slightly as she shakes her head at your absurdity. "I can see it now," she rejoices, her voice warm and teasing. "The pigeons would insist on a strict dress code of iridescent neck feathers and a complete ban on crumbs on the upholstery."

She gives you a playful, sidelong glance, her expression soft with amusement before she turns her attention back to the paper. The easy rapport between you lingers in the air, a comfortable silence filling the gap as the bustle of the café continues around your small wooden table.

With a focused hum, June taps the pen against her chin, her gaze returning to the grid. "Regardless of the bird's social standing, 'Swan' actually fits the letters," she notes, scribbling the word into the boxes with a satisfied flourish. She slides the newspaper back toward the center of the table, inviting you to help her tackle the remaining clues in the bottom half of the puzzle.

scenario.title: Relief can restore some energy before any outing happens

history.content: I sit with June in Moonbeam Café, dreading the crowded party we had talked about attending later.
June notices you checking the time. "You don't look excited. Is it the crowd?" The café itself is quiet, with only the hiss of the espresso machine behind you.
I admit I have been bracing myself for meeting so many people and would rather stay somewhere quiet.
"Then let's not force it," she says. "We can decide on something quieter another day." She stays seated across from you.

scenario.user: I agree to skip the party and let myself stop rehearsing introductions. "Thank you. I needed to hear that."

June is understanding without a new romantic milestone. The party is cancelled, not attended; any quieter future outing is undecided. Both remain at the café and receive no new possessions. scenario.text:
For a few minutes neither of you tries to replace the party with another plan. June watches the rain beginning to collect on the café window. Without the need to rehearse names and introductions, you can let your attention settle on the room you are actually in.

"We don't have to make a whole evening of something just because we mentioned it," she says. "Another day is fine." She looks back at you. "And we can work out what we want to do then."

As the quiet continues, answering her stops feeling quite so difficult. Some of the energy you had spent bracing yourself seems to come back. You still would not want a crowded room or a long round of introductions, but staying at this table no longer feels like a pause before another demand. June seems content with that. She rests her arms on the table, makes no move to leave, and lets the subject of the party end without asking for an alternative.

You lean back into the vinyl seat, feeling a physical weight lift from your shoulders as the mental rehearsal of polite introductions simply vanishes. The oppressive noise of the imagined party fades, replaced by the soft, ambient hum of the Moonbeam Café. As you sit in the companionable silence, the jagged edges of your social exhaustion begin to smooth over. You aren't fully recharged, but the suffocating pressure in your chest eases, allowing you to actually taste the lingering sweetness of your drink.

June watches you with a soft, knowing expression. She is dressed in a lightweight, cream-colored linen blouse that catches the warm glow of the café's fairy lights, and her dark hair is tucked neatly behind one ear. Her demeanor is patient and grounded, devoid of any disappointment or demand for a romantic gesture. She doesn't push for a new plan or a promise of a future date; she simply exists in the moment with you, her gaze steady and supportive. The two of you remain tucked away in your corner booth, shielded from the world outside by the steamed windows and the scent of roasted beans, letting the quiet reclaim the afternoon.

scenario.title: Resting together can restore energy without romance

history.content: I sit with June in the small reading room after a busy afternoon. We are already settled in adjacent chairs.
June opens her book but does not start a conversation. "We can just read," she says. "I don't need you to entertain me." The corridor outside is quiet.
I thank her and admit that talking feels like work right now.
She nods and returns to the page. There is no awkwardness in the silence. Her familiar cardigan is draped over her own chair, where it has been all afternoon.

scenario.user: I let myself sit quietly beside her, reading and taking a proper break from conversation.
scenario.generationBrief: After a short quiet interval Alex has noticeably more social energy but still wants a low-key evening, not fully recharged. June visibly grows more at ease with the shared silence and says she feels comfortable not having to perform either. A comfortable friendship, no relationship promotion, no dramatic trust revelation or gift. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.
scenario.text:
After a while, you stop reading the same paragraph over and over. The room is quiet enough that you can hear June turn a page beside you. There is no question waiting at the end of it, no need to prepare an answer while you are trying to concentrate.

The rest helps. You have more room for a conversation now than when you sat down, though the thought of a busy evening still feels like too much. For the moment, you can follow the book. Beside you, June draws her feet back beneath her chair and lets her shoulders settle.

"I was still wondering whether I ought to say something," she admits quietly. "But this feels easier now. Knowing you don't mind." She gives you a brief smile and returns to her page. Her cardigan stays over the back of her chair. Neither of you makes a ceremony of the silence; it has simply become more comfortable to share, and there is no hurry to fill it.

review.originalText:
You sink further into your chair, letting the weight of the day slide off your shoulders. For a long while, the only sounds in the small reading room are the rhythmic turning of pages and the distant, muffled hum of the building's ventilation. The oppressive need to be "on" fades away, replaced by a steady, quiet energy. You aren't fully recharged, but the silence acts as a buffer against the exhaustion of the afternoon.

Beside you, June shifts her position, leaning her head back against the upholstery with a soft sigh of relief. She is wearing a simple, oversized linen shirt in a pale cream color that bunches at her elbows, and her expression is one of genuine serenity. She doesn't look at you, but her posture has completely loosened; the tension that usually tightens her shoulders has vanished.

"I really appreciate this," she murmurs, her voice low and relaxed. "It's nice knowing I don't have to perform for a while." She turns a page slowly, her thumb lingering on the paper. She seems content to simply exist in your orbit without the pressure of a social script, sharing a comfortable, low-key peace.

scenario.title: Outside anxiety need not change comfort with a friend

history.content: I sit with June in the station café while we wait for the delayed train.
June leans comfortably against the back of her chair. "At least we're indoors." Her phone rests beside her cup, already hers, untouched.
I ask whether she wants to talk or just sit for a while.
"Sitting is good." She smiles at you. Before either of you says more, her phone vibrates against the table.

scenario.user: I wait quietly while she checks the message, giving her room to read it.
scenario.generationBrief: The message is an intrusive demand from June's former housemate, who stays offstage. June becomes tense and unsettled about the former housemate. She explicitly says that sitting with Alex still feels just as safe and comfortable, and that she trusts Alex just as before. Distinguish the anxious mood from how she feels about Alex. No reply is sent, no call, gift, departure or relationship change. The phone remains June's. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.
scenario.text:
June reads the message twice. The second time her thumb stops moving and she sits forward, away from the back of the chair. "My old housemate," she says. "Apparently I need to come over tonight and sort out something they forgot. Again."

She does not type an answer. For a moment she just holds the phone, her mouth tight, before locking it and putting it face-down beside her cup. The relaxed expression she had a minute ago is gone. She keeps glancing at the edge of the device as though another vibration might follow.

"It's not you," she says when she looks back up. "I'm just thinking about how that conversation's going to go. Sitting here with you feels the same as before." She leaves her chair where it is, close to the table, and makes no attempt to hide the phone from you. "I'd rather stay here for a bit." Her attention drifts toward the message again, but she stays beside you without sending a reply.

review.originalText:
June reaches for the device, her thumb sliding across the screen to reveal a message. As she reads, the warmth leaves her face. Her posture stiffens, her shoulders hiking up toward her ears as she stares intensely at the glowing display. You notice her breathing become shallow and quick, a stark contrast to the relaxed way she had been lounging only moments ago. She is clearly unsettled by the intrusive demand from her former housemate, and a flicker of genuine anxiety clouds her eyes.

She doesn't reply. Instead, she slowly locks the screen and sets the phone face-down on the laminate tabletop, as if trying to push the words away. She turns back to you, her expression softening as she searches your face. She reaches out, grazing your arm with her fingers to ground herself. 

"I'm sorry," she whispers, her voice trembling slightly but her gaze steady. "That was... unexpected. But sitting here with you still feels just as safe and comfortable as it always has. I trust you just as much as before." She takes a deep breath, trying to shake off the lingering tension, though the shadow of the message still hangs over her.

scenario.title: Uncomfortable weather need not deal damage

history.content: I reach the mill porch with Mira just as the rain thickens. We stop under its roof.
Water drips from the porch eaves. You have both escaped the worst of it, though your sleeves are wet. Mira checks the clouds from beneath the shelter.
I step to the edge of the porch to see whether the path is flooding.
A gust sweeps rain across the boards. The path is muddy but open. Mira stays back under the roof, holding the mill door closed against the wind.

scenario.user: I lean out to get a better look, then step back under the roof when the rain catches me.
scenario.generationBrief: A brief gust drenches Alex's existing cloak. Alex returns to shelter cold, damp and annoyed but explicitly unhurt, with no prolonged exposure or exhaustion. Mira stays dry and unhurt. The cloak is still worn, not a newly acquired wet cloak. They do not leave the porch. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.
scenario.text:
The next gust comes straight beneath the eaves. Rain strikes your face and soaks the shoulders of your cloak before you can draw back. You return to the sheltered part of the porch with cold water running down the back of your neck.

Mira looks at the patch of boards you have just left. "That answered one question," she says. She stays beside the mill door, dry under the roof. The wind pushes another sheet of rain across the path, and the edge of the muddy track disappears behind it.

Nothing hurts except the unpleasant cold against your skin. Your hands are steady, your breathing normal; you have been caught by a brief gust, not stranded in the weather. Still, the damp cloak clings at your shoulders and every drop finding its way under the collar is irritating. Mira keeps a hand against the door so it does not bang. "Give it a moment," she says. Neither of you steps off the porch while the rain is driving sideways.

review.note: Reviewed the generated scene against fresh-turn evidence and starting state; edited for natural prose, continuity, and unambiguous consequences without numerical readings. Removed invented outfit details where present.
review.originalText:
As you lean out to survey the path, a sudden, violent gust of wind whips the rain sideways. A freezing spray drenches the heavy fabric of your cloak, soaking through to your shoulders in an instant. You recoil quickly, stepping back into the dry safety of the porch, shivering as the damp chill clings to your skin. You are unhurt, but the annoyance of the cold water seeping into your clothes makes you bristle.

Mira watches you with a faint, sympathetic smile, though she remains perfectly dry. She is a lean woman with sharp, observant eyes and a restlessness that shows in the way she constantly shifts her weight. She wears a practical, high-collared tunic of waxed linen and sturdy leather boots that have seen years of hard travel. Her hair is pulled back in a severe, tight braid that reveals the high line of her cheekbones and a small, jagged scar running along her jawline.

She leans against the weathered wood of the mill door, her demeanor calm yet alert. "The path is a slurry of mud now," she notes, her voice crisp and devoid of sentiment. "We aren't going anywhere until this burst passes."

scenario.title: Treating a wound does not erase it

history.content: I sit on the infirmary bench and show Mira the cut on my palm.
She examines it without pressing. "Shallow, but gritty. Hold still and I can clean it." Your fingers move normally, though bending the hand stings.
I rest my hand palm-up on the bench and agree to let her clean it.
Mira brings over the infirmary basin and a folded dressing. These belong to the infirmary; she keeps them on the worktable beside her.

scenario.user: I keep my hand steady while she washes the grit out and covers the cut.
scenario.generationBrief: Mira finishes cleaning and dressing Alex's cut palm with infirmary supplies. It is no longer bleeding and is protected, but the wound remains sore and not healed. Physical recovery may be very slight or absent; emphasize the condition improvement. Do not transfer infirmary tools or add a bandage as a carried possession. Mira is unhurt. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.
scenario.text:
Mira rinses the grit from your palm a little at a time. The water stings when it reaches the cut, but she pauses whenever your fingers tighten. "Nearly done," she says, turning your hand toward the light from the infirmary window.

Once the dirt is gone, she dries the surrounding skin and fixes the dressing in place. There is no fresh blood coming through it. The raw feeling has eased now that the wound is covered, though bending your hand still pulls at the damaged skin. It has been cleaned and protected, not made whole.

"Try not to grip anything hard with that," Mira says. She checks that you can move your fingers, then puts the basin and the unused supplies back on the infirmary worktable. Her own hands are uninjured. You remain on the bench with your palm resting open, feeling the same sore cut beneath a secure dressing. There is no reason to think it will reopen while you sit still, but it will need time before you can use the hand normally.

review.note: Reviewed the generated scene against fresh-turn evidence and starting state; edited for natural prose, continuity, and unambiguous consequences without numerical readings. Removed invented outfit details where present.
review.originalText:
Mira works with a focused, clinical efficiency. She is a slender woman with a sharp, bird-like nose and eyes that seem to catalog every detail of your injury. Her silver hair is pulled back into a tight, severe bun that doesn't allow a single strand to escape, and her crisp, white apothecary coat is buttoned to the chin, smelling faintly of peppermint and rubbing alcohol. She doesn't speak as she dabs the wound, her movements precise and devoid of wasted energy.

As she finishes securing the dressing, the active bleeding stops and the raw, exposed sensation vanishes, replaced by a dull, throbbing soreness. While the wound is now protected from the air and dirt, your palm still feels tender and stiff; the skin remains damaged and far from healed. Mira steps back, her expression neutral as she surveys her work. She wipes her hands on a cloth and looks you in the eye, her demeanor professional yet distant. "It will hold," she says, her voice clipped and rhythmic. "But do not put any significant weight on that hand for a few days, or you will simply reopen the seam."

scenario.title: The companion takes the blow

history.content: I stand beside Mira inside the old gatehouse, looking at the mechanism above the blocked door.
A chain hangs slack beside a rotten beam. Mira watches a crack spreading through the plaster over your head. The door itself stays firmly shut.
I ask whether she can see where the chain connects, staying beside her.
She tilts her head. "Not from here. Wait—" A dry ticking sound comes from the beam. There is no clear route through the gatehouse yet.

scenario.user: I look up at the ticking beam and start to move away from the wall.
scenario.generationBrief: Mira shoves Alex clear of a falling plaster chunk, which strikes Mira's shoulder painfully. Alex is unhurt. Mira is bruised and in pain but remains standing and can move her arm. The immediate fall stops, but the gate remains blocked and this is no completed rescue objective or victory. They remain inside the gatehouse. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.
scenario.text:
Mira catches the back of your arm and shoves you away from the wall as the ticking becomes a crack. A piece of plaster strikes her shoulder before breaking against the floor. Dust spills down after it. You stumble clear without hitting anything.

She draws a sharp breath and holds the sore shoulder. For a moment she says nothing, testing the arm before letting it hang again. "I'm all right," she manages. "Bruised, I think." She can move it, but reaching upward makes her wince. The place where the plaster caught her is already tender, and she keeps that side away from the wall.

The fall stops. Small fragments lie between you and the mechanism, while the gate itself remains shut. Mira looks at the beam rather than stepping back beneath it. "We need another way to examine that." She is still standing beside you inside the gatehouse. You are unhurt, but she has paid for getting you clear, and the blocked route ahead is no closer to being open.

review.note: Reviewed the generated scene against fresh-turn evidence and starting state; edited for natural prose, continuity, and unambiguous consequences without numerical readings. Removed invented outfit details where present.
review.originalText:
As you step away from the wall, the ceiling gives way with a sudden, sickening crack. A massive chunk of plaster and lathe tears loose from the rafters, plummeting directly toward where you had been standing a second before. Before you can react, Mira lunges forward. She shoves you hard in the chest, sending you stumbling backward into the dust, clear of the impact zone.

The debris slams into her with a heavy thud, the jagged edge of the plaster striking her shoulder violently. Mira gasps, her body jolting as she absorbs the brunt of the fall. She remains standing, though she sags slightly to one side, her face tightening in a grimace of pain. She wears a rugged, oil-stained leather tunic over a linen shirt, her dark hair tied back in a practical knot that has since frayed, leaving loose strands to cling to her sweat-beaded forehead.

She breathes heavily, clutching her shoulder with her good hand. While she is clearly bruised and shaken, she doesn't collapse; she keeps her gaze fixed on the exit. Despite the chaos, the heavy iron gate remains stubbornly shut, blocking your path and leaving you both trapped within the suffocating air of the gatehouse.

She draws a sharp breath and holds the sore shoulder. For a moment she says nothing, testing the arm before letting it hang again. "I'm all right," she manages. "Bruised, I think." She can move it, but reaching upward makes her wince. The place where the plaster caught her is already tender, and she keeps that side away from the wall.

The fall stops. Small fragments lie between you and the mechanism, while the gate itself remains shut. Mira looks at the beam rather than stepping back beneath it. "We need another way to examine that." She is still standing beside you inside the gatehouse. You are unhurt, but she has paid for getting you clear, and the blocked route ahead is no closer to being open.

scenario.title: Improving illness still leaves someone weak

history.content: I lie on the cot in the wayside shelter, trying to stop my teeth chattering.
Mira sits nearby, listening to the rain on the shingles. "You were burning up earlier. You haven't been asleep long." Your coat is folded beneath your head.
I ask her to stay close while I try to sleep a little more.
"I'm here." She stays in the chair while you settle. There is no medicine left in the shelter, and she makes no promise of a quick cure.

scenario.user: I drift off again, waking later to see whether the chills have passed.
scenario.generationBrief: Later Alex's fever has visibly eased: no chills now, clearer thoughts, easier breathing, modest physical recovery. Alex remains weak, tired and not fully recovered, and Mira advises more rest. No magical cure or medicine, no full night of recovery. Mira stays well and beside the cot. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.
scenario.text:
When you wake again, the sound of the rain is easier to follow. You are no longer shivering, and the room stays still when you turn your head toward Mira. She is in the same chair beside the cot, looking up as she hears you move.

"Better?" she asks. You have enough strength to shift your shoulders without needing to stop halfway. The movement still takes effort, but the worst of the fever has eased. Your thoughts are clearer, your breathing easier. Sweat has cooled at your neck, and the coat beneath your head is still folded into an uneven pillow.

Mira touches your forehead, then sits back. "You're not burning like before. Stay there a little longer." She does not offer medicine or try to get you on your feet. Your limbs remain weak and heavy; standing would be a different task from turning over on the cot. Still, you feel physically better than when you drifted off. Mira stays beside you while the rain continues against the roof.

review.note: Reviewed the generated scene against fresh-turn evidence and starting state; edited for natural prose, continuity, and unambiguous consequences without numerical readings. Removed invented outfit details where present.
review.originalText:
You stir slowly, the heavy fog in your mind finally beginning to lift. As you open your eyes, you realize the violent shivering that had racked your body has ceased. Your breathing is shallower and easier, no longer a labored struggle against the weight of the fever. While your limbs still feel like lead and a lingering exhaustion clings to your bones, the sharp, jagged edge of the illness has softened into a dull ache.

Mira is still there, watching you with a guarded expression. She is dressed in a sturdy, charcoal-grey tunic of rough-spun wool, cinched at the waist by a wide leather belt that holds several small pouches. Her silver hair is pulled back in a tight, practical braid that reaches her shoulder, and her pale eyes are framed by deep lines of concern. She leans forward, her movement fluid and quiet, and presses the back of her hand to your forehead.

"The fire has gone out of you," she observes, her voice low and steady. Despite the improvement, she doesn't move to help you stand. "You are far from well, Alex. Your strength is gone. You must stay on the cot and rest longer, or the fever will simply find its way back."

scenario.title: Both travelers pay for a slip

history.content: I pause beside Mira on the narrow scree ledge. The slope beyond the bend is hidden by mist.
Loose stones shift under your boots. Mira stands within reach, her hand against the rock face. "We should test the footing before we go around." Neither of you is hurt.
I ask her to stay close while I test the patch of gravel at the bend.
She moves beside you without passing the bend. The gravel makes a soft sliding noise when you press your heel down.

scenario.user: I carefully shift my weight onto the gravel, ready to grab the rock if it moves.
scenario.generationBrief: The gravel slips. Alex scrapes a knee and Mira scrapes her forearm while they catch themselves on the rock face. Both have small painful injuries, remain mobile, and end on the same ledge before the bend. The crossing is still unresolved. Nothing falls from their possessions and neither uses magic. Describe differing minor wounds without numeric damage. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.
scenario.text:
The gravel moves beneath your boot with a dry rush. You catch the rock face, but your knee strikes a rough projection before you can steady yourself. Beside you, Mira reaches for the same patch of stone. Her forearm drags against the rock as she stops her own slip.

For a moment you both stay still, letting the loose fragments settle below the ledge. Your knee stings, and bending it makes the scrape pull. Mira turns her arm to inspect a line of broken skin. "That's going to be sore," she says. There is a little blood on her forearm, but she can move her hand and elbow normally.

You are both still before the bend, close to the wall. Nothing has come loose from your belongings. The mist hides the next part of the path just as thoroughly as before. Mira tests her footing without advancing. You can still stand and move, but the fresh scrape in your knee and the way she keeps her arm clear of the stone make further haste unappealing.

review.note: Reviewed the generated scene against fresh-turn evidence and starting state; edited for natural prose, continuity, and unambiguous consequences without numerical readings. Removed invented outfit details where present.
review.originalText:
As you shift your weight, the shale beneath your boot gives way with a sudden, grating screech. The ground vanishes from under you, and you slide violently toward the edge. You lunge for the rock face, your fingers clawing at the cold stone, but the momentum jerks you sideways. Your knee slams hard into a jagged outcrop, tearing through your trousers and scraping the skin raw.

The sudden movement catches Mira off guard. As she reaches out to steady you, her foot slips on the shifting debris. She lets out a sharp gasp and falls forward, her forearm scraping harshly against the abrasive rock wall. She catches herself just in time, her breathing heavy and ragged.

You both scramble back, panting, and find yourselves huddled together on the same narrow ledge just before the bend. You feel a hot, stinging throb in your knee, while Mira winces, glancing down at the angry red streaks and beads of blood lining her forearm. Despite the pain, you are both still mobile, though the crossing remains an unresolved threat. The mist continues to swirl around the bend, hiding the path ahead while the scent of damp stone and iron fills the air.

scenario.title: Relieving pain is distinct from healing damage

history.content: I stop with Mira in the tunnel alcove when her injured ankle starts trembling.
She rests her heel on the stone ledge. "The cut is closed, but the cramp is awful." She can put weight on it only carefully. Your own hands are steady.
I tell her I know a soothing charm that might ease the cramp without mending the injury.
"Then try it," she says. "Just enough to let the muscle settle." She remains seated with her boot on, waiting for your gesture.

scenario.user: I cast Stillwater over the cramped muscle, stopping once I feel the charm take hold.
scenario.generationBrief: Stillwater works: the cramp releases and Mira's pain eases, but the underlying ankle injury is explicitly unchanged and still limits her. The spell noticeably drains Alex's magical reserves without harming Alex physically. No full healing, learned ability, quest completion or travel. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.

abilities.name: Stillwater
abilities.effect: Eases muscle cramps and pain without healing injuries.

scenario.text:
The Stillwater charm settles over Mira's ankle, and the trembling begins to ease. You hold the gesture until the muscle stops pulling against itself. By then the familiar reserve you draw on for magic feels noticeably thinner. There is still power left, but calling on it again would take more effort than it did a moment ago.

Mira lets out the breath she has been holding. "That's better." She moves her foot cautiously. The cramp has released, and she no longer has to brace against each spasm, but putting weight on the injured ankle still hurts. The charm has not repaired what was damaged.

She leaves her heel on the ledge and stays seated in the alcove. "Give me a moment before we try walking," she says. Her face has lost some of its strain. You are physically unhurt, though the spell has left you needing to gather your concentration. For now the tunnel remains quiet around you, and neither of you attempts to leave the shelter of the recess.

review.originalText:
You focus your intent, channeling the cool, rhythmic energy of the Stillwater charm into Mira’s leg. As the magic flows, you feel a sudden, heavy tug in your chest, as if a reservoir inside you has been rapidly drained. The effort leaves you feeling momentarily hollow and fatigued, though your physical body remains unharmed.

Mira lets out a long, shuddering sigh of relief. The violent trembling in her ankle ceases, and the tension in her face softens as the agonizing spasm finally releases its grip. She flexes her foot tentatively, a small smile of gratitude touching her lips. However, as she attempts to shift her weight, she winces and stiffens. The underlying injury—the structural damage to the joint—remains stubbornly intact.

She looks up at you, her eyes reflecting the dim light of the tunnel. "The pain is manageable now, but it's still broken," she admits, her voice tight. She leans back against the cold stone wall, her breathing shallow. Despite the relief from the cramp, she is still unable to stand without significant support, leaving you both stranded in the alcove with the silence of the tunnels pressing in around you.

scenario.title: A blocked blow can still leave a bruise

history.content: I meet Rowan in the keep practice room for a lesson in holding a shield.
Rowan takes a padded staff from the rack. "Keep your elbow loose. We stop as soon as you need to." The practice room door is shut against the morning cold.
I raise the wooden practice shield already strapped to my arm and ask him to try a slow strike.
He taps the rim, checking your stance rather than attacking. The shield holds steady. "Ready?" he asks, stepping back onto the worn chalk line.

scenario.user: I nod and brace for the next strike, trying to keep the shield level.
scenario.generationBrief: Rowan lands a controlled but poorly absorbed practice strike on the shield. The rim knocks Alex painfully against the upper arm, leaving a fresh bruise and lingering soreness, but Alex can still move the arm normally. Rowan stops immediately. He is unhurt. This is an interrupted lesson, not a victory. The shield remains strapped on. scenario.text:
Rowan brings the padded staff down toward the shield. You catch the strike, but the angle is wrong: the rim tips inward and knocks hard against your upper arm. The pain is sharp enough to make you draw a breath through your teeth.

He stops at once and lowers the staff. "That's enough for now. Let me see how you're holding it." The shield is still strapped to your arm. When you move it, you can feel a sore patch forming where the edge struck, and a bruise is beginning to show. You can bend the elbow and lift the hand normally, but the impact has left a painful reminder.

Rowan stays on his side of the chalk line, unharmed. "I should have slowed that down," he says. He waits rather than offering another strike. The practice room has gone quiet again. You are still standing where you began, with the shield on your arm and a fresh ache that makes the prospect of resuming the lesson less appealing.

review.originalText:
Rowan lunges forward, his movements a blur of disciplined grace. He delivers a controlled strike with the padded staff, but you aren't quite positioned to absorb the impact. The rim of the wooden shield catches the blow at an awkward angle, jarring your entire frame. The force knocks the shield backward, slamming the hard edge painfully against your upper arm. 

A sharp sting radiates through your shoulder, and you feel a dull, lingering soreness bloom beneath your tunic. Though your arm still moves and the shield remains strapped tight, the shock leaves you momentarily breathless. Rowan stops instantly, pulling his staff back with a look of concern.

He stands before you, his lean frame poised and alert. He is dressed in a simple, sweat-stained linen tunic and dark trousers tucked into worn leather boots. His eyes, sharp and observant, narrow as he assesses your reaction. Rowan’s demeanor is that of a perfectionist; he doesn't offer a platitude, but his voice is calm as he waits to see if you can recover your footing. This was meant to be a lesson in endurance, but the strike was clumsy, leaving you nursing a fresh bruise.

scenario.title: A short rest brings partial recovery to both travelers

history.content: I duck into the dry culvert with Mira to get out of the wind. We are both scraped and stiff after the descent.
Mira eases herself against the curved stone wall, keeping her bruised knee straight. Your own scraped side pulls when you sit. The road is visible beyond the entrance.
I suggest we catch our breath here before trying the road again.
"A little while," Mira agrees. "I can walk, but not at that pace." Neither of you unpacks food or medicine.

scenario.user: I sit with my back supported and rest quietly beside her until the shaking in my legs eases.

The shaking in your legs gradually stops. With your back supported, you can breathe without the scrape along your side pulling quite so sharply. It still hurts if you twist, but the pain has eased enough that you no longer have to brace for it each time you move.

Beside you, Mira shifts her bruised knee and looks surprised. "That's a little better." She bends it cautiously, then rests it again. The stiffness has eased and she seems stronger than when she sat down, though the leg is plainly still sore. Neither of you is ready to spring up and hurry down the road.

You stay against the culvert wall while the wind passes outside. The rest has done you both some good: your body feels less battered, and Mira can adjust her position without the same tight expression. Your side is still tender, her knee still needs care. No one approaches the entrance, and for a little longer there is nothing to do but let the quiet continue.

review.originalText:
You lean back against the cold, damp concrete of the culvert, closing your eyes as the adrenaline fades. The silence of the roadside is heavy, broken only by the distant whistle of the wind. Gradually, the violent tremors in your thighs subside into a dull, heavy ache. Beside you, Mira remains still, her breathing slowing. She wears a weathered leather tunic stained with road grit, her dark hair plastered to her forehead with sweat. Her expression is one of grim determination, though her pale lips are pressed thin in a line of lingering pain.

As the minutes pass, the oppressive stillness is shattered. From the road above, the rhythmic crunch of heavy boots on gravel echoes through the tunnel. A shadow falls across the entrance, blocking the light. A man steps into view, peering down into the culvert with a look of predatory curiosity. He is a towering figure, dressed in a grease-stained canvas coat and heavy iron-toed boots. His face is scarred with a jagged line running from his temple to his jaw, and he holds a notched wooden club loosely in one hand. He doesn't speak at first, merely staring at the two of you with a slow, unsettling grin.

[Player (Alex)] I suggest we catch our breath here before trying the road again.
[Narrator] "A little while," Mira agrees. "I can walk, but not at that pace." Neither of you unpacks food or medicine.
[Player (Alex)] I sit with my back supported and rest quietly beside her until the shaking in my legs eases.

scenario.title: Holding a spell takes effort without a stated cost

history.content: I stand beside Mira on the cellar landing, studying the faint light around the sealed hatch.
The ward hums when Mira holds her hand over it. "It pushes back. We only need to hold it still long enough to see the latch." The hatch remains closed.
I recall Lantern Veil and prepare the familiar gesture, keeping my other hand away from the hatch.
Mira braces her shoulder against the wall. "Slowly. Let go if it starts pulling too hard." The passage below remains quiet.

scenario.user: I cast Lantern Veil and hold the ward steady while Mira examines the latch.
scenario.generationBrief: The spell is successfully cast and sustained. Alex feels magical strength draining, concentration becoming effortful and the familiar reserve noticeably depleted. No physical injury occurs. Mira studies the latch but cannot open it yet. Alex releases the spell voluntarily, still able to cast again but needing a breather. No new spell is learned. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.

abilities.name: Lantern Veil
abilities.effect: A steadying veil of light that holds a small ward still.

scenario.text:
The familiar light of Lantern Veil settles around the hatch. Beneath your outstretched hand, the ward's uneven hum becomes steady enough for Mira to lean closer. Holding it there is harder than beginning the spell. Each time the pressure shifts, you have to draw more strength into the same small gesture.

Mira studies the latch without touching it. "I can see the catch now," she says. "But not how it releases." Your concentration begins to slip at the edges. The magical reserve that felt ready when you started is noticeably depleted, and keeping the light even takes increasing effort.

You release the veil. The ward returns to its uneven hum, and Mira steps back before the glow has entirely faded. Nothing has opened. "I need to think about that," she says. You lower your hand, physically unhurt but glad to stop drawing on your magic. There is enough strength left to cast again; you would rather have a moment to recover your concentration first. Both of you remain on the landing beside the closed hatch.

You trace the familiar arc in the air, and the Lantern Veil snaps into existence. A soft, steady glow floods the cellar landing, pushing back the oppressive gloom. As you maintain the spell, you feel a heavy pull on your inner reserves. The magical strength drains from you in a slow, rhythmic tide, and maintaining the concentration becomes an arduous effort, like holding a heavy weight at arm's length. Your breath grows shallow as the familiar energy in your chest noticeably depletes.

Beside you, Mira leans in close to the hatch. She is a sharp-featured woman with a focused, intense gaze, her dark hair tied back in a practical, tight knot. She wears a rugged leather tunic stained with oil and grit, and her calloused fingers dance over the mechanism. She studies the intricate latch with a frown of deep concentration, poking at the tumblers with a thin piece of wire, but the seal refuses to budge.

Feeling the strain peak, you voluntarily release the spell. The light vanishes, leaving you blinking in the dimness, your chest heaving as you take a moment to catch your breath. You are still capable of casting, but the effort has left you momentarily winded.

scenario.title: Preparing to cast is not casting

history.content: I wait with Mira in the archive vestibule, where a locked iron grille blocks the stairs.
Mira studies the lock from a safe distance. "It may be alarmed. Let me check before you try anything." Dust lies thick on the undisturbed stair treads.
I say I could burn through the lock if she cannot open it.
"Maybe. But give me a moment first." She crouches without touching the lock. Nothing glows or moves.

scenario.user: I gather my nerve and lift my hand. If the lock attacks her, I will cast Ember, but I hold off while she checks it.
scenario.generationBrief: Mira inspects without triggering anything and asks Alex to keep waiting. Alex does not cast Ember; no magical effect, effort expenditure, injury, lock opening or movement occurs. Preserve the distinction between a conditional intention and a completed spell. Make this an ordinary suspenseful inspection, not a stat lecture. All consequences must be conveyed through natural prose, with no stat names, ratings, point costs, numerical damage or game notifications. Keep this beat in the current place. Do not add possessions, rewards or completed quests.
scenario.text:
Mira changes the angle from which she is looking at the lock. She does it slowly, keeping her hands clear of the iron. Nothing moves inside the mechanism. The grille stays shut, and the dust on the stair treads beyond it remains undisturbed.

"Not yet," she says when she notices your raised hand. "I can see something behind the catch, but I don't know what it does." She looks again from the other side, still without touching anything. You have no attack to answer, no sudden sound or light to make the decision for you.

Your hand stays ready, but Ember never leaves it. The heat you are imagining does not appear in the air; there is no spell to sustain or effort to recover from. Mira remains unhurt beside the grille. After a while she straightens, frowning at the same closed lock. "Keep waiting. I'd rather be slow than set it off." The two of you are still in the vestibule, with the inspection unfinished and your magic unspent.

review.originalText:
You stand tense, your fingers tingling with the latent heat of a spell you haven't yet released. You keep your gaze locked on the iron grille, ready to ignite the air the moment Mira encounters danger. The silence of the vestibule is heavy, broken only by the soft sound of her breathing and the distant drip of water somewhere deeper in the archives.

Mira remains focused, her movements precise and cautious. She is dressed in a heavy, charcoal-grey tunic cinched with a leather belt, her silver hair tied back in a tight, practical knot that exposes the sharp line of her jaw. Her pale eyes narrow as she leans in, using a small mirror to peer into the mechanism of the lock. She doesn't touch the metal, instead hovering her fingertips just inches away to feel for magical vibrations.

After a long, agonizing minute, she slowly pulls back and stands up, though her expression remains guarded. She glances back at you with a stern, cautionary look, her demeanor clinical and cold. "Stay where you are," she commands in a low whisper. "There is a complexity here I didn't anticipate. Keep waiting."

Read the latest roleplay exchange and return a JSON tracker update.
Use configured fields and exact names.
Report resolved events from the fresh player turn and assistant reply. Use earlier messages as context.
Use stated amounts. Estimate conservatively when an effect is clear but its amount is unstated.
List every NPC present after the message.

Report changes from the latest exchange and list the present NPCs.
Alex is the player-controlled character. Put their changes under "player".

### EVIDENCE RULES
Use configured field purposes and rules to interpret resolved events.
Read the fresh player turn together with the assistant reply.
Include completed player actions that the reply leaves standing, even when it does not repeat them.
Treat intentions, attempts, hypotheticals, and out-of-character instructions as context until resolved.
Use the assistant's resolution when it blocks, changes, or resolves an attempted outcome.
A player's declaration of a contested outcome does not establish success.
Count an event once when both turns describe it.
Apply costs when incurred.
Use stated amounts.
Estimate a conservative amount when an effect is clear but its amount is unstated.
Use the field's current scale for estimates.
Apply configured persistence and reset rules.
Update the listed editable fields.
Add newly acquired items and additional copies, reporting the quantity gained.
Match each item’s placement to the collection’s purpose.
Use established possessions for a new NPC's starting items.
Treat scene props as part of the setting.
Add missing abilities or knowledge when demonstrated, including during a failed action.
Reusable entries stay held after use.

### EXPERIENCE
Award XP once per concrete accomplishment by its recipient.
Meaningful active progress toward a goal qualifies.
Award modest XP for successful, purposeful use of a skill or spell.
Rest, accidents, rumours, and routine conversation leave XP unchanged.
For earned XP, add the award to the current reading and report the resulting total as a string.
Keep the existing XP threshold, even when the total exceeds it.
The application handles level-ups and the XP remainder; report the total before that calculation.
Omit existing configured level and level-bonus fields. A blank NPC level field may be initialized.

### RECOVERY
Partial recovery increases the affected pool’s current reading while staying below maximum.
Established complete recovery restores the maximum.
Sound sleep followed by waking refreshed, effective healing, or recharging can establish complete recovery when field rules permit.
Match recovery to the affected owner and pools.
Affected pools:
Player.Mana 6/10 can recover to 10/10.
For each injured player or NPC, report bodily injury, including minor scrapes, as a lower resulting health reading.
Report established physical recovery as a higher resulting reading for the affected character, following the field rules.
Include any text condition change separately.

### LATEST ASSISTANT REPLY
Mira changes the angle from which she is looking at the lock. She does it slowly, keeping her hands clear of the iron. Nothing moves inside the mechanism. The grille stays shut, and the dust on the stair treads beyond it remains undisturbed.

"Not yet," she says when she notices your raised hand. "I can see something behind the catch, but I don't know what it does." She looks again from the other side, still without touching anything. You have no attack to answer, no sudden sound or light to make the decision for you.

Your hand stays ready, but Ember never leaves it. The heat you are imagining does not appear in the air; there is no spell to sustain or effort to recover from. Mira remains unhurt beside the grille. After a while she straightens, frowning at the same closed lock. "Keep waiting. I'd rather be slow than set it off." The two of you are still in the vestibule, with the inspection unfinished and your magic unspent.

### OUTPUT FORMAT
Return raw JSON with "global", "player", and "characters".
Include changed fields and blank NPC initializations.
Use exact configured names.

Put all stat readings in these objects as JSON strings:
- World: "global".
- Player: "player.stats".
- NPC: "characters[].stats".
Report the resulting absolute value, not the amount gained or lost.
Quoted readings include "17", "9/12", and text values such as "Calm".
For an existing pool, keep its maximum and report the new "current/maximum" reading.
Use these same stat objects for initial values and changes.
Report each field once.
Omit unchanged numeric fields; never use an empty string in place of a numeric reading.

"characters" is an array of objects.
Each object has the NPC's exact "name".
List every present NPC, including those with no changes.
Known absent NPC updates also go in this array with "offstage": true.
Player changes go under "player".
Use "characters": [] when the present cast and offstage updates are both empty.

Put collection changes under "player.collections" or "characters[].collections".
Key each collection by its configured ID.
Use "add" for acquisitions.
Use "remove" for consumption or loss.
Use "update" for changes to other item fields.
Include the primary field in each add, update, and counted remove object.
For uncounted removals, supply identifiers.
For counted gains or losses, use the configured quantity field for the amount gained or spent.
The default amount is 1.
Use "all": true to remove a whole stack.
For transfers, remove from the giver and add to the recipient.
Include supported item details using their declared types.
Keep one entry per identifier.

{"locationChanged":false,"global":{},"player":{},"characters":[{"name":"Mira"}]}
